chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Wassafi, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is pleased if Allah were to extend his lifespan and expand his sustenance, let him maintain goodly relations with his kin, for the kinship has a tongue on the Day of Resurrection, eloquent, saying: O Lord! Maintain relationship with the one who maintained it with me, and cut off the one who cut me off.'
So the man would be seen to be on the goodly way, when the kinship that he had cut off comes to him, so it would plunge with him into the lowest depth into the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of maintaining family ties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores silat al-rahim as a divine mechanism for sustaining worldly blessings, linking physical longevity and material provision to spiritual fidelity. The metaphor of the womb's 'eloquent tongue' (lisān dhallāq) personifies kinship as an active intercessor on the Day of Judgment, reinforcing the concept that severing ties invites immediate spiritual descent to the lowest depths of Hell (asfal al-ārfīn).
